root_cause_of_the_import_failure.what: Graph.lower_to_top_level_ir builds the signature as `params_shapes + inputs_shapes` and then binds each PlaceholderOp to the next argument **in body order**. The rewrite inserted its new int8 and scale parameters at the first compute node -- which is after the graph inputs -- so the inputs were bound to weight-shaped arguments and a [2048] quantised buffer ended up where the cache position belongs.
root_cause_of_the_import_failure.why_the_tool_did_not_catch_it: tools/triton_call_replace.py lowers through GraphDriver, which builds subgraphs and binds arguments differently; the same graph lowered fine there while failing through Graph. Reproduced side by side in one process.
fixes: _placeholder_anchor places a new parameter right after the last existing parameter, so the body keeps its 'parameters, then inputs' order
_reindex now emits _fake_params and _inputs sorted by body index, because the insertion order of the new parameters is not their body order

defect_found_and_fixed.symptom: the accumulator was produced by a FullOp (arith.constant)
defect_found_and_fixed.why_it_matters: a constant used as a writable operand makes one-shot bufferize give the call a copy, so writes are lost; and the int8 matmul kernel genuinely accumulates (its TTIR does `tt.load %C` then `tt.dot(a, b, previous)`), so C must start at zero AND be shared
defect_found_and_fixed.fix: Q, activation scale and Out now come from EmptyOp (tensor.empty, which bufferize allocates and shares); the accumulator is a linalg.generic that copies a zero constant into an empty buffer -- a computed value, so it is neither folded back to a constant nor copied on write
defect_found_and_fixed.sub_bug: copy_op's argument order is (destination, source): it builds `linalg.generic ins(args[1]) outs(args[0])`. I had them the other way round, which copied the uninitialised buffer into the constant.
